text: Legacy AC3 of RWB-E3-020 is kept word for word with its origin tag even though it tests R-DIS-01, the vehicle repossession rule, which belongs to RWB-E3-019.
why: The split rule requires every legacy criterion to be copied verbatim to the story that owns it and forbids rewording; the behaviour of R-DIS-01 is delivered by RWB-S5-E3019-APP, so no value and no rule row is duplicated here.
read: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md RWB-E3-020; FSD S5 A2.2.3.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-01 and R-DIS-02
applied_in: RWB-S5-E3020-APP s7 and s8; RWB-S5-E3020-CON s19
impact: The deed in lieu story carries one criterion whose behaviour is proved by the sibling vehicle story; the rule set of the feature is tabled once and no duplicate build is scheduled.

text: The registered deed in lieu transfer is consumed on RWB-S2-E3012-CON, class C, with a placeholder operation name, and its fake is available on Day 1.
why: Architecture v5 gives the agreement to rwb-treatment and no rwb-asset event carries the registered transfer; a contract dependency never blocks an app build, so the story starts on the published document and its fake.
read: Architecture v5 slide 41; slide 19 IN; FSD S5 A2.2.2; WP B2-S5-002 story JSON
applied_in: RWB-S5-E3020-APP s3, s4 and s12.2; RWB-S5-E3020-CON s3, s12.2 and s12.8
impact: The take-on step is blocked by no other team; the operation name stays a placeholder until rwb-treatment publishes it and the row is added to the plan as class C.

text: The asset record is read as S5's own table in schema rwb_asset, next to asset_sale and listing, while the Ownership Map lists no asset row.
why: TSD S5 T3.1 defines the asset object with the take-on columns and Architecture v5 slides 19 and 41 give the record to rwb-asset; no other service claims it, and a take-on with no record owner cannot be built.
read: _work/msr/context/S5.md ownership rows; TSD S5 T3.1 and T3.3; Architecture v5 slides 19 and 41
applied_in: RWB-S5-E3020-APP s11 and s12.7; RWB-S5-E3020-CON s3, s7 and s12.7
impact: The DB story of the service creates asset in rwb_asset; if the Ownership Map ruling differs, one migration and the two reads change and no business value moves.

text: The ACE NPA asset and collateral facts are read only through the rwb-source-data data product of DP06 Collateral and assets, with a placeholder operation name and its fake; rwb-asset holds no v_ace_* grant.
why: Architecture v5 allows only rwb-source-data to read the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views and DP-05 forbids any other service from reading an ACE view or table, so the legacy direct reads cannot be carried.
read: Architecture v5 slide 8 note and slides 29, 37 and 45; FSD S5 A2.2.2; DP table DP-05
applied_in: RWB-S5-E3020-APP s3, s11 and s12.2; RWB-S5-E3020-CON s7 and s12.2
impact: The boundary test fails any build that reaches a v_ace_* view; the asset fields the product must carry are listed in the contract baseline.

text: The AssetTakenOn event is published from the outbox of the platform library RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, taken as available, while the metadata row keeps the build dependencies the plan states.
why: A business event must leave from the outbox in the same transaction as the row it announces (DP-09), and the pattern set of this key does not carry the library or its contract story.
read: Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT and slide 43 row 22; DP table DP-09; WP B2-S5-002 story JSON
applied_in: RWB-S5-E3020-APP s12.3 and s13; RWB-S5-E3020-CON s12.3 and s13
impact: The outbox stub stands in on Day 1 and the H row is added in the next plan revision; no event is published outside the outbox.

text: The case move to ASSET_ON_BOOKS is answered as the stage outcome of the child workflow with the rule ID and its version, and rwb-case writes the case row; no published move operation exists.
why: Temporal and Drools Design slide 13 makes every stage a child workflow of CaseWorkflow, and the case and its route states belong to rwb-case; the answer therefore travels on the workflow boundary.
read: Temporal and Drools Design slide 13; TSD S5 T4; FSD S5 A2.2.3.1
applied_in: RWB-S5-E3020-APP s4, s9 and s12.2; RWB-S5-E3020-CON s7 and s12.2
impact: The parent applies the state; if rwb-case publishes a move operation the same answer is re-expressed as that call and no rule changes.

text: Both stories trace to REQ-S5-001 of the Business Requirements Program v4 until the split plan allocates a requirement id to this legacy key.
why: No requirement id is allocated to the slice and a story with no traceability row is not accepted by the review, while the program requirement states exactly what the feature delivers.
read: Business Requirements Program v4; TSD S5 T8; WP B2-S5-002 story JSON
impact: The traceability chain is complete against the program requirement and is re-pointed when the plan allocates the id.

text: The Land Office registration is kept outside every service and is read as the registered transfer fact of RWB-S2-E3012-CON and as an officer step.
why: No service or integration id covers the registration, and the feature needs only the fact that ownership passed to the bank with its date and book value.
read: FSD S5 A2.2.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-02; Epics 3 to 8 Specification FEAT-AST-02
impact: No build is scheduled for the registration; the date it produces is written to DF-COL-036 and no service claims the step.
